title: One-dimensional arrays: indexing, filtering, and search
goal: Connect every index to a valid range and distinguish storage capacity from logical length.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.standard-sequences. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: The object and its elements
paragraphs: int values[4]{} creates four zero-initialized ints with indices 0,1,2,3. Four is the count, not the final index. A built-in array’s bound in ordinary C++ must be a constant expression; int a[n] with a runtime n is not a standard solution.

Use vector for a changing size, or a fixed buffer with a separate count<=capacity. {} initialization never permits access beyond the array. All buffer elements exist, but only the first count may represent task data.

sections.title: Arrays in parameters
paragraphs: An int a[] parameter is adjusted to int*, so the declaration does not carry the length into the function. sizeof that parameter measures a pointer. Do not derive length using sizeof(a)/sizeof(a[0]) inside such a function.

Pass span<const int> or an explicit pointer/length pair with a proven contract. Here span preserves bounds. At the actual array declaration, sizeof applies to the array, but a clear interface remains preferable.

sections.title: Capacity and length
paragraphs: Process only the first count elements in a fixed array.

sections.title: Linear search
paragraphs: Search left to right, comparing each element with the target. Return the first matching index. If none matches, return a separate flag or size() as an end position; callers must check that result before indexing.
An empty range has no match. Duplicates require a policy: first, last, or all indices. The lab counts qualifying elements, so each visited index contributes once even when values repeat.

sections.title: Stable filtering
paragraphs: To select nonnegative values, traverse the input and append qualifying values to a new vector. Relative order is preserved, and an empty result is valid. Sum only selected values; do not confuse an element count with a sum of indices.

In-place filtering can use a write index with write<=read: read the original element before writing a selected one. That requires another invariant. Begin with two containers so memory optimization does not obscure correctness.

sections.title: The first match
paragraphs: size represents no match and is never dereferenced.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.
Trace state after each significant operation and identify the established preconditions.
Run the source, compare stdout and exit code, then check the additional cases.

sections.title: Minimum and empty input
paragraphs: An empty range has no minimum. Do not initialize the minimum to zero when all values may be positive. After checking nonemptiness, start with the first element and compare the rest; a later structure can carry an explicit presence flag.
For n<=100 and |value|<=1000, the absolute sum is at most 100000. For a[i], establish both i<count and count<=capacity. The compiler is not required to diagnose a violation.

sections.title: Comparing representations
paragraphs: The same span-based algorithm should return identical results for int[], array, and vector. Ownership, resizing, and interfaces differ, not the sequence’s mathematical meaning. Avoid coupling a computation to a global buffer.

Test an empty set, one negative value, one zero, all selected, none selected, and duplicates. Record expected order and count for each. Next, add a second coordinate while explicitly checking matrix shape.

selfcheck.prompt: What does a search index equal to size() mean?
options: An end position that must not be dereferenced
selfcheck.feedback: Only indices below size() are valid.

selfcheck.prompt: What is the final index of four elements?
Does an empty set have a minimum?
selfcheck.feedback: Do not read a[0] before checking nonemptiness.

selfcheck.prompt: Does sequential filtering with push_back preserve order?
selfcheck.feedback: Each accepted element is appended after the previous one.

practice.title: Laboratory: One-dimensional arrays: indexing, filtering, and search
practice.task: Select nonnegative values from n<=100 integers in -1000…1000, preserving order. Print count sum, then selected values separated by spaces; an empty result has an empty second line.
criteria: The contract matches the task and defines units, empty input, and extra data.
Every published case matches and two explained original tests are included.
A data length must accompany element access.
Do not initialize a minimum from a[0] before checking nonemptiness. Do not use a VLA as standard C++20.
Source, actual output, exit code, and a justified complexity explanation are preserved.
